messages:
maria: Acme support case — intermittent GitHub OAuth failures. Users hit "invalid_request: state_mismatch" on callback. Seems to happen more in Chrome. Customer route: GitHub -> sso.acme.com (corporate redirector) -> our callback. Can we triage?

kevin: any example logs or redirect chain from the customer?

maria: pasted error log from their repro run:

  ERROR oauth: callback failed user=alice@acme error="state mismatch"
  GET /oauth/callback?code=Splx...&state=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...%2Babc

kevin: are there any middleboxes (CDN/edge worker) or analytics redirectors that could change query params?

maria: customer says their enterprise SSO redirector (sso.acme.com) wraps external OAuth flows to add tracking. They provided a curl -I -L output.

ryan: possible parameter collision — if their redirector appends its own `state` (for tracking) after decoding the `to=` param, it can overwrite our original state token. Does the curl output show duplicated/overwritten state?

maria: yes — here's the core of the redirect chain they sent:

  HTTP/1.1 302 Found
  Location: https://sso.acme.com/redirect?to=https%3A%2F%2Flogin.redwood.ai%2Foauth%2Fcallback%3Fcode%3DSplx...%26state%3DeyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...%252Babc

  HTTP/1.1 302 Found
  Location: https://login.redwood.ai/oauth/callback?code=Splx...&state=tracking_12345

kevin: that lines up — their redirector decodes the `to=...` then appends `state=tracking_12345` instead of preserving the encoded `state`. Our server receives `state=tracking_12345` and rightly rejects the request.

ryan: extra gotcha: Chrome sometimes normalizes `+` to space if a param is decoded twice during a redirect chain. Combined with the redirector's append, the original signature can be corrupted.

maria: here's the exact curl they used to reproduce locally:

  curl -v -L 'https://sso.acme.com/redirect?to=https%3A%2F%2Flogin.redwood.ai%2Foauth%2Fcallback%3Fcode%3DSplx...%26state%3DeyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...'

kevin: mitigation options we can propose to the customer:
  - ask them to configure the redirector to preserve existing query parameters on the `to=` target (don't append `state`).
  - ask them to append their tracking param under a different name (e.g., `acme_track`) so it won't collide.
  - we could add support for an alternate fallback param on our side (e.g., `rdr_state`) behind a feature flag, but that is a product change and requires careful security review.
  - temporarily loosening state enforcement for that client_id is possible but HIGHLY discouraged.

ryan: action for eng: I will instrument a `state_overwrite_detected` log when the incoming callback `state` does not match the expected token we issued (only emit metadata — never log the actual token). I'll also prototype support for an alternate param name behind a feature flag so we can evaluate impact without changing default behavior.

maria: action for support: ask Acme SRE to change their redirector config to preserve query params or rename their tracking param. I'll send a sample patch/NGINX snippet they can use.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for feature/logging change at 02:00 UTC tomorrow (window requested by eng). :rocket:

maria: thanks — will follow up with customer and confirm when they test. :thumbsup:

kevin: marking this thread for follow-up. Close once Acme confirms redirector change or we have feature-flagged fallback in canary.
